ingredients: 2 fluid ounces bourbon whiskey, or more to taste
instructions: Place egg yolks in a saucepan. Whisk in sugar until well blended and creamy. Add milk and cream; whisk until blended. Place pan over medium heat; whisk frequently until mixture reaches a temperature of between 170 to 180 degrees F (75 to 80 degrees C) using an instant-read thermometer. Remove from heat. Stir in nutmeg and whiskey.
Chill pan in cold water until cool. Transfer mixture to a container (a large pitcher is ideal). Cover and refrigerate until thoroughly chilled, 2 to 3 hours.

Place egg whites in a bowl and whisk until soft peaks form. Add sugar and continue whisking until egg whites hold a firmer peak. Whisk egg whites into custard base until thoroughly blended. Refrigerate until chilled, about 30 minutes.
Whisk eggnog again just before serving and between each pour to ensure even distribution of the egg whites which tend to float to the top. Serve with a dusting of nutmeg.

1619.title: Hot Toddy Cocktail
1619.description: The hot toddy cocktail is a classic winter warmer. It's good any time of year and works particularly well if you're battling a cold.
instructions: Fill an Irish coffee glass with hot water; let sit for a few minutes until glass is hot, then discard water.
Pour honey and bourbon into the preheated glass and top with 3/4 cup hot water. Garnish with a lemon twist.

1620.title: Jack Daniel's Very Merry Eggnog
1620.description: Don't wait for December to enjoy this Jack Daniel's eggnog! Make Thanksgiving festive with this deliciously potent, quick and easy, homemade eggnog recipe.
ingredients: 1 pinch ground nutmeg, or to taste
instructions: Mix sugar, rum, bourbon, brandy, vanilla, nutmeg, and salt in a blender on medium speed until combined. Transfer to a large bowl.
Pour half-and-half, cream, and eggs into the blender; mix on low speed until combined. Carefully pour into the liquor mixture and stir to combine.
Ladle combined mixture back into the blender in batches; blend on low speed. Transfer blended eggnog to a punch bowl or pitcher.
Refrigerate eggnog until cold, 1 to 2 hours, before serving.

1621.title: Chef John's Whiskey Sour
1621.description: Homemade simple syrup and the addition of an egg white makes Chef John's best whiskey sour recipe a tasty, summer-ready, go-to cocktail that's sure to please!
ingredients: 1 fluid ounce freshly squeezed lemon juice
4 drops orange bitters, or more to taste
instructions: Prepare simple syrup: Bring sugar and water to a simmer in a small pan over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until sugar is dissolved. Pour into a small bowl and let cool completely before using, 15 to 20 minutes.

Make cocktail: Pour 3/4 fluid ounce simple syrup, bourbon, lemon juice, bitters, and egg white into a large cocktail shaker. Cover with a smaller cocktail shaker, or top, and give cocktail a "dry shake" without ice, about 30 seconds.

Add 3 ice cubes to bourbon mixture, cover, and shake vigorously until the shaker is very cold and the outside is frosty, about 45 seconds. Uncover and strain into a rocks glass containing 1 large ice cube.

1622.title: Kentucky Derby Bourbon Punch
1622.description: Bourbon is the star ingredient in this Kentucky Derby punch that also includes orange juice and lemonade for a refreshing adult beverage.
ingredients: 1 (12 fluid ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed
1 (12 fluid ounce) can frozen lemonade concentrate, thawed
instructions: Mix bourbon, orange juice concentrate, lemonade concentrate, lemon juice, and maraschino cherry juice together in a pitcher until base is well mixed.
Pour base into a punch bowl; add club soda, lemon slices, and maraschino cherry halves.

1623.title: Strawberry Basil Bourbon Smash
1623.description: Strawberries and fresh basil are smashed together until fragrant in this bourbon-based cocktail perfect for summer.
ingredients: 0.25 cup fresh strawberries, cut into chunks
3 fluid ounces sparkling water, or as needed
instructions: Muddle strawberries, lemon juice, basil, and simple syrup together in a cocktail glass until smashed together and fragrant. Add bourbon and ice; stir to combine. Top with sparkling water.

1624.title: Autumn Sunshine Cocktail
1624.description: Enjoy this golden sunshine cocktail made with maple syrup, Grand Marnier, and bourbon, garnished with fresh clementine peel for autumn in a glass.
ingredients: 1 fluid ounce brandy-based orange liqueur (such as Grand Marnier®)
1 clementine, juiced and peel cut into 1x1/4-inch strips
instructions: Place ice cubes in a shaker. Pour bourbon, maple syrup, orange liqueur, clementine juice, and lemon juice over ice. Cover the shaker and shake until chilled, about 15 seconds. Strain into a chilled martini glass.
Light a match or lighter over the cocktail and squeeze 1 piece of clementine peel near the flame to flame the oil. Rub peel on the rim of the glass and drop peel into the cocktail.

1625.title: Jim Beam Black Hot Toddy
1625.description: Honey, sugar, and lemon juice combine with a full-bodied whiskey to create a hot toddy recipe that'll warm you up from the inside out.
instructions: Put bourbon, lemon juice, and honey in a 6-ounce mug.
Top off with hot water and stir until honey is dissolved.
Garnish with a lemon peel (optional).

1626.title: Simple Mint Julep
1626.description: Mint, bourbon, and sugar are mixed with ice in this classic mint julep recipe that is quick and easy to prepare for the Kentucky derby.
ingredients: 5 fresh mint leaves, or to taste
1 (1.5 fluid ounce) jigger bourbon, or more to taste
instructions: Place a tall glass in the freezer until frosted.

Mix water and sugar together in the frosted glass until sugar is dissolved. Twist mint leaves to release the scent and flavor from each leaf; add to glass. Fill the glass 1/4-full with bourbon; add ice. Garnish the glass with mint leaf.

1627.title: Jim Beam® Yule Nog
1627.description: Rich, creamy eggnog is the base of this tasty yule log cocktail that tastes just like the holidays made with Jim Beam®.
instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with a dusting of fresh ground nutmeg.

1628.title: Jim Beam Apple Highball
1628.description: Nothing is more refreshing on a clear fall day than an apple highball cocktail made with premium whiskey.
instructions: Fill a tall highball glass with ice. Add bourbon and soda water. Garnish with a lemon wedge.

1629.title: Holiday Manhattan
1629.description: This recipe is definitely not traditional - except in my family. It is sweet, and meant to be! You will have to do the math for single servings, this is the way I got it from my Grandfather, who always made a batch (or two) for the Holidays.
instructions: Dissolve the sugar in hot water in a large pitcher. Stir in the whiskey, vermouth, cherry juice and bitters. Serve in glasses over ice and garnish with a maraschino cherry.

1630.title: Jim Beam Black® Manhattan
1630.description: Dress up after-dinner drinks with a Jim Beam Black® Manhattan cocktail, worthy of a black-tie affair.
ingredients: Cherries or lemon peel, for garnish
instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice in a mixing glass.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with a cherry and/or lemon peel.

1631.title: Cider-Bourbon Thermos Cocktail
1631.description: Whether served hot or cold, this easy thermos cocktail with apple cider, tea, and bourbon is perfect for chilly nights.
instructions: Bring cider and maple syrup just to a boil in a saucepan. Remove from heat. Add tea bags, ginger, and cardamom. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Remove and discard tea bags and spices. Stir in bourbon and lemon juice.
Transfer to a warmed 32- to 40-ounce thermos.

1632.title: Clementine Old Fashioned
1632.description: This easy old fashioned cocktail is made with the juice of fresh clementines, but can be made with nectarines, oranges, or other fruit of your choice.
instructions: Strain clementine juice into an old fashioned glass. Add bourbon, lemon juice, and simple syrup. Add ice, stir to chill, and serve.

1633.title: Betty's Famous Eggnog
1633.description: This rich eggnog is made the old-fashioned way by blending beaten egg yolks, whipped egg whites, sugar, and heavy cream with bourbon, rum and brandy. A dusting of nutmeg accents the creamy flavors.
instructions: Beat the eggs and sugar together in a very large bowl until thick and light-colored. Stir in the bourbon and rum, mixing until sugar has dissolved. Let stand about 1 hour.
Meanwhile, whip the egg whites in a separate bowl until stiff peaks form.

Stir the whipping cream and half and half into the egg yolk mixture until thoroughly blended. Slowly stir in the brandy. Fold in the egg whites, blending evenly. Cover and refrigerate two hours before serving. May be stored in the refrigerator up to one week.
Serve in small cups or glasses dusted with a pinch of nutmeg.

1634.title: Frozen Derby Mint Juleps
1634.description: Perfect for Derby Day or any day spent lounging in the sun, these frozen mint juleps are quick and easy to make and refreshingly delicious.
instructions: Pour bourbon, lemon juice, simple syrup, and mint leaves into a blender; blend on high until combined. Add ice; blend until juleps have a slushy consistency. Divide among serving glasses.

1635.title: Bourbon Cider Sour
1635.description: Spruce up a basic whiskey sour by turning it into a bourbon cider sour with Jim Beam® Bourbon, apple cider, and orange juice.
instructions: Combine the bourbon, apple cider, orange juice, and simple syrup. Stir.
Serve with an apple slice.

1636.title: Blackberry-Mint Julep Margarita
1636.description: The Kentucky Derby meets Cinco de Mayo in this refreshing blackberry-mint julep margarita cocktail that will surely delight you and your guests.
ingredients: 6 leaves fresh mint, plus more for garnish
instructions: Muddle blackberries and mint in a shaker. Add bourbon, tequila, lime juice, and agave nectar.
Fill shaker with ice. Shake and strain into two julep glasses filled with fresh ice.

1637.title: Ginger-Peach Smash
1637.description: You'll become a bourbon lover after sipping on this refreshing ginger-peach smash cocktail, muddled and garnished with mint.
ingredients: 4 sprigs fresh mint, divided, or as needed
0.75 fluid ounce ginger liqueur (such as Domaine de Canton®)
instructions: Muddle 5 to 8 mint leaves, depending on size, with peach nectar in a cocktail shaker until leaves are broken down, about 1 minute.
Pour in bourbon and ginger liqueur and fill the shaker with ice. Close and shake until well chilled. Strain into a rocks glass with a large whiskey ice cube.
Lightly slap 2 sprigs of mint between your hands to release their scent, then garnish the drink with them.

1638.title: Christmas Cheer
1638.description: Spiced apple cider with a hint of bourbon is a warm way to spend the Christmas season.
ingredients: 4.125 inch piece fresh ginger, cut into thin slices
instructions: Tie cloves, cardamom pods, allspice berries, and star anise together in a cheesecloth sachet.
Combine apple cider, cranberry juice, and brown sugar together in a pot; bring to a simmer. Add cinnamon sticks, ginger, and spice sachet to cider mixture and steep for 20 minutes.
Pour 1 fluid ounce bourbon into each mug and top off with spiced cider. Rub the edge of each mug with orange peel and drop into the drink.

1639.title: John Collins Cocktail
1639.description: John Collins seizes the spotlight from his more famous brother, Tom, in this quick and easy, super refreshing carbonated whiskey cocktail!
ingredients: 0.25 cup club soda, or as needed
instructions: Fill a chilled cocktail glass with ice; add whiskey and lemon juice. Stir in sugar until dissolved. Top off with club soda. Garnish with lemon slice.

1640.title: Lemonade with Whiskey
1640.description: This delicious adult beverage combines those perennial favorites -- lemonade and whiskey -- to kick off your summer party!
ingredients: 1 (6 ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed and undiluted
1 (6 ounce) can frozen lemonade concentrate, thawed and undiluted
1 (2 liter) bottle lemon-lime flavored carbonated beverage, chilled
instructions: Combine bourbon, orange juice concentrate, lemonade concentrate, and lemon juice in a large pitcher and mix well. Chill for at least 3 hours.
Add lemon-lime beverage and club soda to the pitcher and mix. Pour over crushed ice to serve.

1641.title: Delicious O.J. Punch
1641.description: Orange juice, bourbon and lemon-lime soda are stirred together in this quick, easy, and quite tasty punch. I have never had a complaint about this one.
ingredients: 1 (12 fluid ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed
instructions: In a punch bowl or other large container, combine the orange juice concentrate, whiskey and lemon-lime soda. Stir until mixed, then throw in some ice before serving.

1642.title: Spiced Pear Old-Fashioned
1642.description: This old-fashioned with rosemary and pear is the perfect fall cocktail.
ingredients: 0.5 fluid ounce ginger liqueur (such as Domaine de Canton®)
instructions: Muddle chopped pear, 1 rosemary sprig, lemon twist, maple syrup, and bitters in a cocktail shaker with a muddler or the handle of a wooden spoon until pear is liquified. Add bourbon, ginger liqueur, and 1 cup ice to the cocktail shaker. Cover and shake until well chilled.

Place large ice cube into the rocks glass and set a small fine sieve over the glass. Strain the drink through the cocktail shaker top and the sieve to catch any large pieces of pulp or rosemary. Top with club soda. Garnish with pear wedge and rosemary sprig.

1643.description: The old fashioned cocktail can be made with bourbon, rye, or blended whiskey. Serve over ice and garnish with an orange slice and a maraschino cherry.
instructions: Pour simple syrup, water, and bitters into a whiskey glass; stir to combine. Add ice cubes and pour in bourbon. Garnish with orange slice and maraschino cherry.

instructions: Muddle sugar cube, water, and bitters in an old fashioned glass for 1 minute. Pour in whiskey; stir for 1 minute.
Squeeze lemon twist over the glass and drop it in. Add ice cubes. Garnish with orange slice and maraschino cherry; serve with a swizzle stick.

1646.description: The John Collins cocktail is made with bourbon instead of gin. It's flavored with lemon and topped up with club soda for a tall, iced cocktail.
instructions: Combine bourbon, lemon juice, and simple syrup in a cocktail shaker. Add 1 cup ice, cover, and shake until chilled. Strain into a Collins glass. Add 1 cup ice, fill with club soda, and stir.
Garnish with orange and lemon slices and a maraschino cherry.

1647.title: Maker's Mark Old Fashioned
1647.description: Straightforward and timeless, this Maker's Mark old-fashioned cocktail never goes out of style: a simple mix of bourbon, bitters, and sugar.
instructions: Muddle sugar, bitters, orange, cherry, and water in an old-fashioned glass.
Remove the orange rind and fill the glass 3/4 full of ice.
Add Maker's Mark Bourbon and stir.

1648.title: Mint Juleps
1648.description: Minty simple syrup mixed with bourbon becomes a refreshing mint julep with this simple recipe. It's a favorite for when you're watching the Kentucky Derby!
ingredients: 0.5 cup roughly chopped fresh mint leaves
8 cups crushed ice, or as needed
instructions: Make the simple syrup: Bring water, sugar, and chopped mint to a boil over high heat in a small saucepan. Cook, stirring occasionally, until sugar is completely dissolved, 1 to 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and let cool for 1 hour. Pour syrup through a strainer to remove mint leaves.
Make the cocktails: Fill eight glasses with crushed ice; pour 4 ounces bourbon and 1/4 cup mint syrup into each cup. (Add extra syrup for anyone with a sweet tooth.) Top each drink with a mint sprig.

1649.title: Bourbon Slush
1649.description: A fruity blend of juices, tea and bourbon whiskey are frozen into a slush, and then served topped off with lemon lime soda. This takes a while, but it's worth it!

1 (2 liter) bottle lemon-lime flavored carbonated beverage

1650.description: Perfect for sipping on cold winter nights, this traditional hot toddy recipe combines all the warming flavors you love--bourbon, honey, and cinnamon.
instructions: Heat water in a glass measuring cup in the microwave for 2 minutes.

Place honey in a large mug. Add hot water and bourbon; stir until honey is dissolved. Squeeze lemon wedge into the mug and discard. Stir with cinnamon stick; leave in the mug. Drop the thin slice of lemon into the mug for garnish.

instructions: Place ice into a shaker.
Pour bourbon and vermouth over ice; shake well.
Pour into a cocktail glass and garnish with a cherry.

1652.description: Two classic bourbon-based drinks come together in this recipe for an old-fashioned Manhattan.

1 fluid ounce orange-flavored liqueur (such as Cointreau®)

Pour honey and bourbon into the preheated glass and top with 3/4 cup hot water. Garnish with a lemon twist.

1656.description: Homemade simple syrup and the addition of an egg white makes Chef John's best whiskey sour recipe a tasty, summer-ready, go-to cocktail that's sure to please!
ingredients: 1 fluid ounce freshly squeezed lemon juice
4 drops orange bitters, or more to taste
instructions: Prepare simple syrup: Bring sugar and water to a simmer in a small pan over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until sugar is dissolved. Pour into a small bowl and let cool completely before using, 15 to 20 minutes.

Make cocktail: Pour 3/4 fluid ounce simple syrup, bourbon, lemon juice, bitters, and egg white into a large cocktail shaker. Cover with a smaller cocktail shaker, or top, and give cocktail a "dry shake" without ice, about 30 seconds.

Add 3 ice cubes to bourbon mixture, cover, and shake vigorously until the shaker is very cold and the outside is frosty, about 45 seconds. Uncover and strain into a rocks glass containing 1 large ice cube.

1657.title: Kentucky Derby Bourbon Punch
1657.description: Bourbon is the star ingredient in this Kentucky Derby punch that also includes orange juice and lemonade for a refreshing adult beverage.
ingredients: 1 (12 fluid ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed
1 (12 fluid ounce) can frozen lemonade concentrate, thawed
instructions: Mix bourbon, orange juice concentrate, lemonade concentrate, lemon juice, and maraschino cherry juice together in a pitcher until base is well mixed.
Pour base into a punch bowl; add club soda, lemon slices, and maraschino cherry halves.

1658.title: Strawberry Basil Bourbon Smash
1658.description: Strawberries and fresh basil are smashed together until fragrant in this bourbon-based cocktail perfect for summer.
ingredients: 0.25 cup fresh strawberries, cut into chunks
3 fluid ounces sparkling water, or as needed
instructions: Muddle strawberries, lemon juice, basil, and simple syrup together in a cocktail glass until smashed together and fragrant. Add bourbon and ice; stir to combine. Top with sparkling water.

1659.title: Autumn Sunshine Cocktail
1659.description: Enjoy this golden sunshine cocktail made with maple syrup, Grand Marnier, and bourbon, garnished with fresh clementine peel for autumn in a glass.
ingredients: 1 fluid ounce brandy-based orange liqueur (such as Grand Marnier®)
1 clementine, juiced and peel cut into 1x1/4-inch strips
instructions: Place ice cubes in a shaker. Pour bourbon, maple syrup, orange liqueur, clementine juice, and lemon juice over ice. Cover the shaker and shake until chilled, about 15 seconds. Strain into a chilled martini glass.
Light a match or lighter over the cocktail and squeeze 1 piece of clementine peel near the flame to flame the oil. Rub peel on the rim of the glass and drop peel into the cocktail.

1660.title: Jim Beam Black Hot Toddy
1660.description: Honey, sugar, and lemon juice combine with a full-bodied whiskey to create a hot toddy recipe that'll warm you up from the inside out.
instructions: Put bourbon, lemon juice, and honey in a 6-ounce mug.
Top off with hot water and stir until honey is dissolved.
Garnish with a lemon peel (optional).

1661.title: Simple Mint Julep
1661.description: Mint, bourbon, and sugar are mixed with ice in this classic mint julep recipe that is quick and easy to prepare for the Kentucky derby.
ingredients: 5 fresh mint leaves, or to taste
1 (1.5 fluid ounce) jigger bourbon, or more to taste
instructions: Place a tall glass in the freezer until frosted.

Mix water and sugar together in the frosted glass until sugar is dissolved. Twist mint leaves to release the scent and flavor from each leaf; add to glass. Fill the glass 1/4-full with bourbon; add ice. Garnish the glass with mint leaf.

1662.title: Jim Beam® Yule Nog
1662.description: Rich, creamy eggnog is the base of this tasty yule log cocktail that tastes just like the holidays made with Jim Beam®.
instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with a dusting of fresh ground nutmeg.

1663.title: Grilled Peach Bourbon Smash
1663.description: A quick and easy grilled fruit cocktail with muddled mint leaves and grilled peach with ginger ale and bourbon is a perfect summer cocktail.
ingredients: 1 large peach – halved, stone removed, and skin on
4 fluid ounces ginger ale, or as needed
instructions: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate. When the grill is hot, close lid and allow to heat, 5 minutes.

Place peach halves and lemon, cut-side down, in sugar until coated. Place on the grill; cook until fruits are soft, about 5 minutes. Cool on a cutting board, about 1 minute. Cut peach into slices with a knife; reserve 2 for garnish.

Place remaining peach, mint leaves, and simple syrup into a cocktail shaker; juice lemon into the shaker. Gently muddle with a cocktail muddler. Pour in bourbon and ice, cover, and shake until the outside of the shaker has frosted. Strain into a chilled glass; top off with ginger ale, and garnish with grilled peach slices and lemon.

1664.title: Jim Beam Apple Highball
1664.description: Nothing is more refreshing on a clear fall day than an apple highball cocktail made with premium whiskey.
instructions: Fill a tall highball glass with ice. Add bourbon and soda water. Garnish with a lemon wedge.

1665.title: Holiday Manhattan
1665.description: This recipe is definitely not traditional - except in my family. It is sweet, and meant to be! You will have to do the math for single servings, this is the way I got it from my Grandfather, who always made a batch (or two) for the Holidays.
instructions: Dissolve the sugar in hot water in a large pitcher. Stir in the whiskey, vermouth, cherry juice and bitters. Serve in glasses over ice and garnish with a maraschino cherry.

1666.title: Jim Beam Black® Manhattan
1666.description: Dress up after-dinner drinks with a Jim Beam Black® Manhattan cocktail, worthy of a black-tie affair.
ingredients: Cherries or lemon peel, for garnish
instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice in a mixing glass.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with a cherry and/or lemon peel.

1667.title: Cider-Bourbon Thermos Cocktail
1667.description: Whether served hot or cold, this easy thermos cocktail with apple cider, tea, and bourbon is perfect for chilly nights.
instructions: Bring cider and maple syrup just to a boil in a saucepan. Remove from heat. Add tea bags, ginger, and cardamom. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Remove and discard tea bags and spices. Stir in bourbon and lemon juice.
Transfer to a warmed 32- to 40-ounce thermos.

1668.title: Clementine Old Fashioned
1668.description: This easy old fashioned cocktail is made with the juice of fresh clementines, but can be made with nectarines, oranges, or other fruit of your choice.
instructions: Strain clementine juice into an old fashioned glass. Add bourbon, lemon juice, and simple syrup. Add ice, stir to chill, and serve.

1669.title: Betty's Famous Eggnog
1669.description: This rich eggnog is made the old-fashioned way by blending beaten egg yolks, whipped egg whites, sugar, and heavy cream with bourbon, rum and brandy. A dusting of nutmeg accents the creamy flavors.
instructions: Beat the eggs and sugar together in a very large bowl until thick and light-colored. Stir in the bourbon and rum, mixing until sugar has dissolved. Let stand about 1 hour.
Meanwhile, whip the egg whites in a separate bowl until stiff peaks form.

Stir the whipping cream and half and half into the egg yolk mixture until thoroughly blended. Slowly stir in the brandy. Fold in the egg whites, blending evenly. Cover and refrigerate two hours before serving. May be stored in the refrigerator up to one week.
Serve in small cups or glasses dusted with a pinch of nutmeg.

1670.title: Frozen Derby Mint Juleps
1670.description: Perfect for Derby Day or any day spent lounging in the sun, these frozen mint juleps are quick and easy to make and refreshingly delicious.
instructions: Pour bourbon, lemon juice, simple syrup, and mint leaves into a blender; blend on high until combined. Add ice; blend until juleps have a slushy consistency. Divide among serving glasses.

1671.title: Bourbon Cider Sour
1671.description: Spruce up a basic whiskey sour by turning it into a bourbon cider sour with Jim Beam® Bourbon, apple cider, and orange juice.
instructions: Combine the bourbon, apple cider, orange juice, and simple syrup. Stir.
Serve with an apple slice.

1672.title: Blackberry-Mint Julep Margarita
1672.description: The Kentucky Derby meets Cinco de Mayo in this refreshing blackberry-mint julep margarita cocktail that will surely delight you and your guests.
ingredients: 6 leaves fresh mint, plus more for garnish
instructions: Muddle blackberries and mint in a shaker. Add bourbon, tequila, lime juice, and agave nectar.
Fill shaker with ice. Shake and strain into two julep glasses filled with fresh ice.

1673.title: Ginger-Peach Smash
1673.description: You'll become a bourbon lover after sipping on this refreshing ginger-peach smash cocktail, muddled and garnished with mint.
ingredients: 4 sprigs fresh mint, divided, or as needed
0.75 fluid ounce ginger liqueur (such as Domaine de Canton®)
instructions: Muddle 5 to 8 mint leaves, depending on size, with peach nectar in a cocktail shaker until leaves are broken down, about 1 minute.
Pour in bourbon and ginger liqueur and fill the shaker with ice. Close and shake until well chilled. Strain into a rocks glass with a large whiskey ice cube.
Lightly slap 2 sprigs of mint between your hands to release their scent, then garnish the drink with them.

1674.title: Christmas Cheer
1674.description: Spiced apple cider with a hint of bourbon is a warm way to spend the Christmas season.
ingredients: 4.125 inch piece fresh ginger, cut into thin slices
instructions: Tie cloves, cardamom pods, allspice berries, and star anise together in a cheesecloth sachet.
Combine apple cider, cranberry juice, and brown sugar together in a pot; bring to a simmer. Add cinnamon sticks, ginger, and spice sachet to cider mixture and steep for 20 minutes.
Pour 1 fluid ounce bourbon into each mug and top off with spiced cider. Rub the edge of each mug with orange peel and drop into the drink.

1675.title: John Collins Cocktail
1675.description: John Collins seizes the spotlight from his more famous brother, Tom, in this quick and easy, super refreshing carbonated whiskey cocktail!
ingredients: 0.25 cup club soda, or as needed
instructions: Fill a chilled cocktail glass with ice; add whiskey and lemon juice. Stir in sugar until dissolved. Top off with club soda. Garnish with lemon slice.

1676.title: Lemonade with Whiskey
1676.description: This delicious adult beverage combines those perennial favorites -- lemonade and whiskey -- to kick off your summer party!
ingredients: 1 (6 ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed and undiluted
1 (6 ounce) can frozen lemonade concentrate, thawed and undiluted
1 (2 liter) bottle lemon-lime flavored carbonated beverage, chilled
instructions: Combine bourbon, orange juice concentrate, lemonade concentrate, and lemon juice in a large pitcher and mix well. Chill for at least 3 hours.
Add lemon-lime beverage and club soda to the pitcher and mix. Pour over crushed ice to serve.

1677.title: Delicious O.J. Punch
1677.description: Orange juice, bourbon and lemon-lime soda are stirred together in this quick, easy, and quite tasty punch. I have never had a complaint about this one.
ingredients: 1 (12 fluid ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed
instructions: In a punch bowl or other large container, combine the orange juice concentrate, whiskey and lemon-lime soda. Stir until mixed, then throw in some ice before serving.

1678.title: Uncommonly Clyde
1678.description: We invented this drink over the holidays, when we had mounds of homemade cranberry sauce in the fridge. We subbed bourbon and experimented until we arrived at this delicious mix.
ingredients: 0.5 teaspoon brandy-based orange liqueur (such as Grand Marnier®)
instructions: Muddle the crushed ice and cranberry sauce in a rocks glass until the ice has been tinged red. Pour in the whiskey, orange liqueur, bitters, and water. Stir and serve.

1679.title: Rosemary Stinger Cocktail
1679.description: A fresh rosemary simple syrup brings herbal flavor to this citrusy, spicy-sweet, bitter cocktail that's great for sipping on hot summer days.
ingredients: 1.5 fluid ounces amaro liqueur (such as Fernet Branca®)
instructions: Combine water, sugar, and rosemary in a microwave-safe glass jar. Microwave and bring to a boil, about 2 minutes, watching carefully to ensure it doesn't boil over.
Allow to sit for 10 minutes; bring to a boil again. Let syrup sit until cooled, 15 to 20 minutes. Strain out the spent rosemary.

Measure 3 fluid ounces of rosemary simple syrup, ice, bourbon, orange liqueur, amaro liqueur, and lemon juice into a cocktail shaker and mix. Pour into glasses, add bitters to each, and top with a sprig of rosemary and an orange peel strip.

1680.title: The Deb (Peach-Basil Bourbon Smash) Cocktail
1680.description: A homemade fresh peach and basil syrup forms the base for this juicy bourbon cocktail that's a great way to wind down after a busy day.
ingredients: 4 ripe unpeeled peaches, pitted and coarsely chopped
3 sprigs basil, tied together with string
3 dashes aromatic bitters (such as 18.21 Prohibition Aromatic Bitters)
2 fluid ounces lime-flavored sparkling water (such as La Croix®)
instructions: Combine chopped peaches, sugar, water, and 3 sprigs basil in a small pot over medium heat. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until sugar dissolves, about 5 minutes. Cool syrup to room temperature, about 10 minutes. Discard basil sprigs.
Pour syrup into a Mason jar, seal, and refrigerate until completely chilled, about 1 hour.

Measure 3 fluid ounces of syrup and peaches into a cocktail shaker; muddle to break peaches up. Add 4 ice cubes, bourbon, and bitters; cover and shake vigorously until ice is mostly melted. Pour into a chilled 8-ounce glass; add remaining 4 ice cubes. Gently stir in sparkling water. Garnish with a peach slice and basil leaf.

1681.title: Frozen Mint Julep Margarita
1681.description: Two classic cocktails combine for a perfect summertime margarita with the not-too-sweet and not-too-tart taste of a mint julep.
instructions: Bring water and sugar to a boil in a small saucepan. Cook until dissolved, about 1 minute. Turn off heat and add mint sprigs. Steep for 3 minutes as mint syrup cools. Remove and discard mint.
Combine ice, margarita mix, tequila, 1 ounce mint syrup, and bourbon in a blender. Blend until smooth. Pour into 4 glasses.

1682.title: Don's Friend Tonja's Cousin Toni's Boyfriend's Grandmother's Eggnog
1682.description: Tonja was born in the 1940's and this is her cousin Toni's boyfriend's grandmother's eggnog, so I'm guessing this is from the mid-1800's and probably dates much earlier. The original recipe called for half milk and half cream, but I use half and half. Delicious and simple, but be warned, Granny apparently liked a kick! I've made it from scratch and with the modern equivalents and it's fantastic either way. Do yourself a favor and use a mixer for everything. Those who like eggnog LOVE this recipe. I never leave a party with leftovers.
ingredients: 2 teaspoons ground nutmeg, or amount to taste
instructions: In a large bowl, beat the eggs and sugar with an electric mixer until thick and pale, about 5 minutes. Gradually stir in the bourbon, rum, half and half and nutmeg.

In a separate chilled bowl, whip the cream until it can stand in a peak. Fold the whipped cream into the egg mixture. Pour into a plastic container and refrigerate overnight (if possible). Shake the container before serving.

1683.title: Dirty Derby Spritzer
1683.description: This Dirty Derby Spritzer is easy to make with fresh mint, bourbon, brown sugar, and peach-flavored seltzer to create an impressive cocktail for two.
ingredients: 1 (12 fluid ounce) can peach-flavored seltzer water
instructions: Muddle mint and brown sugar in a mixing glass until crushed.
Add bourbon and stir to dissolve sugar. Strain into 2 ice-filled Collins or rocks glasses. Top with seltzer and garnish with peach slices.

1684.title: Hurricane I
1684.description: A large cocktail that contains amaretto, light and dark rum, orange juice and pineapple juice.
instructions: Fill a 16 ounce glass with ice. Pour in amaretto, light rum and dark rum. Pour in orange juice, pineapple juice, and lemon juice. Stir, then top with a dash of grenadine and garnish with an orange slice and a cherry.

1685.title: Texas Hurricane
1685.description: This beverage is known for its 'sneak up and blow you away' power. If you can walk after two of these...well...you just think you can. Everything is bigger and better in Texas -- just try this and see.
instructions: Fill a hurricane glass with ice. Pour in the rum, coconut rum, vodka, gin, triple sec, orange juice, pineapple juice, and grenadine. Stir well with a bar spoon, then pour the 151 rum over the back of the spoon to float the liquor on top of the drink. Garnish the glass with orange, lime, and a cherry.
Sip with a straw from the bottom for a 'sneak up on you' punch or sip from the top for a 'knock you down' twister.

1686.title: Smooth Sweet Tea
1686.description: This sweet tea is a classic Southern drink served chilled and easily made with tea bags and sugar for a great way to cool down on a hot summer day.
instructions: Sprinkle a pinch of baking soda into a 64-ounce, heat-proof glass pitcher. Pour in boiling water and add tea bags. Cover and allow to steep for 15 minutes.
Remove tea bags and discard; stir in sugar until dissolved. Pour in cool water; refrigerate until cold, about 3 hours.

1687.title: Honey Lemon Tea
1687.description: This lemon tea is a sweet and sour tea easily made in the microwave with honey, sugar, and fresh lemon juice that's great for soothing sore throats.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon white sugar, or to taste
instructions: Pour water into a mug. Add honey and heat in the microwave for 1 minute 30 seconds.
Stir in lemon juice, mixing until honey is dissolved. Stir in sugar.

1688.title: Chai Tea Latte
1688.description: Make your own milky chai tea lattes with this homemade recipe that uses boiling water, milk, sugar, honey, and a chai tea bag. Delicious hot or iced!
instructions: Pour boiling water over chai tea bag in a mug; let steep 4 to 6 minutes. Remove and discard tea bag.
Stir honey and sugar into tea to dissolve. Stir milk through tea to serve.

1689.title: Matcha Frappe
1689.description: This recipe, inspired by Starbucks Green Tea Frappuccino®, blends matcha green tea powder, milk, vanilla syrup, and ice for a delicious cold drink.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon matcha green tea powder, or more to taste
1 tablespoon whipped cream, or to taste
instructions: Combine milk, matcha green tea powder, ice, and vanilla syrup, respectively in a blender; blend to desired consistency. Serve with whipped cream on top.

1690.title: Friendship Tea
1690.description: This is a lemony spiced tea mix with cinnamon and clove that makes great gifts during the holidays, or any time!
instructions: In a large bowl, combine instant tea, lemonade powder, orange drink mix, cinnamon and clove. Mix well and store in an airtight container.
To serve, Put 2 to 3 teaspoons of mix in a mug. Stir in 1 cup of boiling water. Adjust to taste.

1691.title: Good Ol' Alabama Sweet Tea
1691.description: This sweet tea is found in houses, churches, and cafes all over the great state of Alabama. If you're north of the Mason-Dixon, you've NEVER had tea this good! Fresh-squeezed lemon, lime, or orange juice can be added for an extra flavor.
ingredients: 3 family sized teabags of orange pekoe tea
3 cups cold water, or as needed
instructions: Pour the sugar into a large pitcher. Bring water to a boil in a large pan. When the water begins to boil, remove from the heat, and place the teabags in. Let steep for 5 to 6 minutes.

Remove tea bags, and return tea to the heat. Bring just to a boil, then pour into the pitcher, and stir until the sugar is dissolved. Fill the pitcher half way with ice, and stir until most of it melts. Then fill the pitcher the rest of the way with cold water, and stir until blended.

1692.title: Honey Milk Tea - Hong Kong Style
1692.description: This sweet milky iced tea is just like what you'd find in a Hong Kong tea shop.
instructions: Steep the tea bags in hot water until the color turns dark red, about 3 to 5 minutes. Discard the tea bags and let the tea cool.

Combine the ice cubes, sweetened condensed milk, and honey in a glass or cocktail shaker. Pour in the tea and mix well. (If the tea is still warm, the ice may melt; add more ice if desired.) A strong, flavorful milk tea is ready for you to enjoy.

1693.title: Tea Punch
1693.description: A different twist to a standard punch. Brewed tea is mixed with orange juice, pineapple juice, lemonade and ginger ale.
instructions: In a pitcher, combine sugar and tea. Stir until sugar is dissolved. Stir in orange juice, pineapple juice and lemonade. Chill in refrigerator for 4 hours.
Just before serving, pour chilled juice mixture into a punch bowl and stir in ginger ale.

1694.title: Homemade Peach Tea
1694.description: Simple, elegant, fresh peach-infused iced tea makes a perfectly sweet summer quaff.
ingredients: 2 slices fresh peach, or more to taste
instructions: Mix 1 cup water, sugar, and peach slices together in a saucepan; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium and simmer, crushing peach slices as you stir, until sugar is dissolved, about 5 minutes. Remove saucepan from heat, cover, and allow peaches to infuse syrup, about 30 minutes. Strain to remove peach slices.
Bring 6 cups remaining water to a boil in a separate pot. Remove from heat, add tea bags, cover, and steep for about 5 minutes.
Remove tea bags from the pot, pour in peach syrup, and cool to room temperature. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

1695.title: Very Popular Bubble Tea
1695.description: Bubble tea is very popular, especially to Asians, but now, more and more people from different backgrounds like the taste of it. I'm no expert at this, but I do know how to make it. It's simple but some of the ingredients may be a little tough to find. Just be patient and look for them in Chinese grocery stores. It is worth the trouble!
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring 2 cups water to a boil. Stir in 1 teaspoon sugar until it dissolves. Toss in the pearl tapioca. Cook for about 20 minutes. Rinse, drain, and refrigerate until chilled.

Pour tea, milk, and 4 teaspoons sugar into a cocktail shaker. Stir until the sugar has dissolved and the milk is well mixed in. Add the ice cubes, and shake so the whole drink can get cold. Pour into a glass, and add tapioca.

1696.title: Caribbean Sorrel Tea
1696.description: Dried sorrel is steeped with ginger, orange zest, and clove then served over ice in this recipe for a unique tea drink from the Caribbean.
instructions: Combine sorrel, ginger, dried orange zest, and clove in a bowl.
Bring water to a boil in a saucepan or kettle; pour over sorrel mixture. Stir in sugar until dissolved. Let mixture steep at room temperature, 8 hours to overnight.
Strain sorrel mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a pitcher; discard solids. Serve over ice.

1697.title: Grandma's Russian Tea
1697.description: This Russian tea recipe with pineapple juice, orange and lemonade concentrates, and warm spices is a perfect treat when you're feeling under the weather.
ingredients: 1 (6 ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate
instructions: Steep tea bags in boiling water until tea is of desired strength, 4 to 5 minutes. Remove and discard tea bags.
Combine 1 1/2 quarts water, cinnamon stick, and cloves in a large pot; bring to a boil.
Add brewed tea, pineapple juice, sugar, orange juice and lemonade concentrates, and allspice to the boiling water; stir until sugar dissolves.
Serve immediately, or reduce heat to low and keep at a simmer until ready to serve.

1698.title: Sweet Lime Iced Tea
1698.description: Not too sweet, not too bitter, this lime tea is just right!
instructions: Pour boiling water into a gallon jar over tea bags. Allow to steep for 45 minutes.
Remove and discard tea bags. Stir in sugar and lime juice until sugar has dissolved. Cool to room temperature; refrigerate until cold before serving.

1699.title: Chai Latte
1699.description: Learn how to make a chai latte with this easy recipe sweetened with sugar and topped with cardamom. If you have an espresso machine, you can steam the goat milk first.
instructions: Place tea bag in a large mug and pour in boiling water. Let steep for 2 to 3 minutes.
Remove tea bag. Stir in milk and sugar; garnish with cardamom.

1700.title: Almond Tea
1700.description: Refreshing almond tea is a wonderful summer treat for parties or just to have on hand when you need an ice-cold beverage.
ingredients: 3 quarts cold water, or as needed
instructions: Mix sugar and instant tea powder together in a 1-gallon container. Pour in boiling water and lemonade concentrate; mix until well combined. Stir in vanilla and almond extracts, then fill the container with cold water. Stir to combine.
Serve over ice or refrigerate until ready to serve.

1701.title: Boston Iced Tea
1701.description: A big pot of tea flavored with cranberry juice. Delicious and refreshing!
ingredients: 1 (12 fluid ounce) can frozen cranberry juice concentrate
instructions: Put water in large pot, and heat on high until boiling. Add sugar and stir until dissolved. Add teabags and let steep until desired strength is acquired. Stir in cranberry juice concentrate, and allow to cool.

1702.title: The Best Lemon Iced Tea
1702.description: This is the best lemon iced tea ever. It comes very close to the Good Host brand Canadians are used to.
ingredients: 10 cups cold water, or as needed
instructions: Place green tea bags and black tea bags in a 1-gallon glass jar or pitcher. Pour boiling water over tea bags; steep for 30 minutes.
Remove tea bags; stir in sugar and lemonade concentrate until dissolved. Stir in lemon juice. Fill jar to the top with cold water. Chill in the refrigerator until cold. Serve over ice.

1703.title: Instant Russian Tea Mix
1703.description: A citrus and spiced dry tea mix that can be given as gifts.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine orange drink mix, sugar, tea powder, cinnamon and cloves. Mix well and store in an airtight container.
To serve, put 3 teaspoons of mix in a mug. Stir in 1 cup boiling water. Adjust to taste.

1704.title: Iced Tea I
1704.description: Like real iced tea, but do you hate boiling the water and then waiting for the tea to cool? Try making it with hot tap water.
instructions: Put tea bags in a 2 quart pitcher. Add hot water. Let sit at least 15 minutes. Add cold water and remove tea bags. refrigerate and serve over ice.

1705.title: Hawaiian Iced Tea
1705.description: Iced black tea accented with pineapple juice shows off its Hawaiian roots and makes a refreshing party drink.
ingredients: 1 fresh pineapple - peeled, cored, and cut into spears
instructions: Pour the barely boiling hot water into a large pitcher, and add the tea bags. Steep the tea, 2 to 4 minutes. Remove the tea bags and pour in the ice water. Pour in the pineapple juice. Refrigerate until thoroughly chilled, about 1 1/2 hours.
Pour the tea over ice, garnish with pineapple spears, and serve.

1706.title: Raspberry Iced Tea
1706.description: Lightly sweetened iced tea gets fruity, refreshing flavors, and a pretty pink color from fresh raspberries and lemonade mix for a perfect summer cooler.
ingredients: 0.5 cup powdered lemonade mix (such as Country Time®)
instructions: Bring the water to a boil in a large pot, and stir in the tea bags, raspberries, and sugar until the sugar has dissolved. Allow the mixture to steep until the desired level of tea flavor is reached, 3 to 5 minutes; remove tea bags, and stir in the lemonade mix until dissolved. Pour tea into pitchers, and add ice to cool.

1707.title: Karkadeh (Egyptian Hibiscus Iced Tea)
1707.description: This traditional Egyptian hibiscus tea is made with loose dried hibiscus flowers and is a great sweet drink to break the fast during Ramadan.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons white sugar, or more to taste
instructions: Place the hibiscus flowers in a pot and cover with boiling water. Sweeten to taste and allow to cool. Strain and pour into a pitcher. Refrigerate until well chilled.

1708.title: Mint Tea Punch
1708.description: Tea, mint, sugar, orange and lemon juices make this a quick and easy, refreshingly delicious drink on a hot summer's day, given to me by a true Southern lady. Goes great with Cajun or spicy foods too. Every time I serve this someone asks me for the recipe!
instructions: Place the tea bags and mint sprigs into a large pitcher. Pour boiling water over them, and allow to steep for about 8 minutes. Remove and discard the tea bags and mint leaves, squeezing out excess liquid. Stir in sugar until dissolved, then stir in the orange juice and lemon juice. Pour in the cold water. Serve over ice cubes, garnished with orange or lemon slices.

1709.title: Homemade Brown Sugar Bubble Tea
1709.description: Cook up dried tapioca pearls (boba) to make this homemade black sugar bubble milk tea sweetened with brown sugar syrup.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons sweetened condensed milk, or to taste
instructions: Bring 2 cups water to a boil in a small saucepan. Add tapioca pearls and stir gently until they begin floating to the top. Reduce heat to medium and simmer until softened and dark, about 25 minutes. Remove from heat, cover, and let sit for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, bring 2 cups water to a boil. Remove from heat and add tea leaves. Let steep for 15 minutes. Strain out tea leaves and refrigerate tea.
Drain pearls. Bring 1/4 cup water to a boil in the empty saucepan. Stir in brown sugar until dissolved. Immerse pearls in syrup and let sit until room temperature, about 15 minutes
Divide pearls and desired amount of syrup between 2 tall glasses. Pour in tea.
Add ice, milk, and sweetened condensed milk to both glasses. Stir before drinking.

1710.title: Rose Hip Iced Tea
1710.description: Rose hip iced tea is refreshingly tart and naturally high in Vitamin C and antioxidants. Try making this easy drink at home.
instructions: Bring water to a boil in a saucepan. Add rosehips to boiling water, cover, reduce heat, and simmer gently for about 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in sugar until dissolved. Leave covered to steep for 5 minutes.
Strain tea through a fine sieve. Cool to room temperature, then transfer to the fridge to chill.

1711.title: Mint Julep Iced Tea
1711.description: Grandma's recipe for citrus tea using homemade simple syrup and mint is a refreshing non-alcoholic version of a mint julep iced tea.
instructions: Bring sugar and 1 cup water to a boil in a small saucepan, stirring until sugar dissolves, about 5 minutes. Add tea bags and mint to sugar mixture; let steep for 10 minutes. Strain mixture and discard tea bags and mint.
Combine tea mixture, cold water, orange juice, and lemon juice in a pitcher.

1712.title: Black Tea Lemonade
1712.description: A very strong, sweet black tea and lemonade mix is sweetened and chilled to make a refreshing summer drink.
instructions: Bring 5 cups of water and the sugar to a boil in a saucepan, then remove from the heat and add the tea bags. Allow tea to steep while you mix the lemonade concentrate and remaining water in a large pitcher. Pour the tea mixture into the lemonade, discarding tea bags. Stir and refrigerate until cold before serving.

1713.title: Mint Garden Tea Concentrate
1713.description: This delicious iced tea is quick, easy, and hits the spot on a hot summer day!
instructions: Bring water to a boil in a large pot. Add mint leaves and steep for 15 minutes. Remove tea leaves from water with a slotted spoon, squeezing leaves to extract any additional liquid; discard leaves.
Stir sugar into steeped tea; return to a boil and cook until sugar is completely dissolved and flavors combined, about 10 minutes. Pour tea concentrate into freezer-safe containers and freeze.

1714.title: South Carolina Sweet Tea
1714.description: Remember, this is the South, where simplicity is the secret to most recipes. Follow this to the 'T' and you will have sweet tea, Sand Lapper (South Carolina) style.
instructions: Using an electric coffee maker, Place the 3 tea bags in the strainer basket (not in the pot). Brew the tea as you would coffee. Pour the sugar in a gallon pitcher. Pour in the hot tea. Continue to run coffee maker with the tea bags until you have enough tea to fill the pitcher. Allow to cool completely at room temperature, then refrigerate.

1715.title: Rhubarb Iced Tea
1715.description: Try making this homemade iced tea infused with rhubarb for a sour kick and a beautiful color when fresh rhubarb is in season.
instructions: Bring 4 cups of water to a boil. Add rhubarb, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes. Remove from heat. Stir in tea bags and mint leaves. Cover and let steep for 30 minutes.
Combine sugar and lemon juice in a pitcher. Strain rhubarb and tea mixture over the sugar. Discard the solids.
Using a wooden spoon, stir tea until sugar has dissolved. Add remaining 4 cups of water to the pitcher and stir again. Serve over ice.

1716.title: Copycat Sweet Iced Tea
1716.description: Just like the sweet tea available at Chick-fil-A®, this copycat version is ultra refreshing and easy to make at home.
ingredients: 0.75 cup white sugar, or to taste
4 cups ice cubes, or as needed
instructions: Combine boiling water, tea bags, and sugar in a bowl. Stir well, cover, and steep for 8 minutes.
Pour cold water into a pitcher. Add hot tea and stir.
Fill 4 glasses with ice cubes. Pour tea over top and serve.

1717.title: Hibiscus Mint Tea
1717.description: This beautiful hibiscus-mint tea is easy to make and tastes delicious whether you serve it hot or cold.
ingredients: 0.5 cup fresh mint leaves, or to taste
1 teaspoon lemon juice, or more to taste
instructions: Fill a stovetop kettle with water and bring to a boil. Remove from heat; add mint leaves, hibiscus petals, and lemon juice. Stir once or twice and cover. Steep for 3 to 5 minutes before serving either hot or iced.

1718.title: Simple Bubble Tea
1718.description: Tapioca pearls, black tea, condensed milk, and sugar are all you need to make your own bubble tea. This recipe is quick, easy, and lots of fun!
ingredients: 4 teaspoons white sugar, or to taste
instructions: Bring water to a boil in a pot, add tapioca pearls, and cover pot. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 5 minutes. Drain pearls and set aside.
Pour brewed tea, condensed milk, and sugar into a pitcher; stir to dissolve sugar. Refrigerate tea mixture until chilled, about 1 hour.
Scoop tapioca pearls into 4 large glasses, about 2 tablespoons each. Fill each glass with tea mixture; top with ice.

1719.title: Kuwaiti Traditional Tea
1719.description: This is the typical tea you will find in regular housed in Kuwait. Its deliciously aromatic and the spices give it a rich taste. You can add/subtract the ingredients to your taste, but be careful with the saffron.
instructions: Combine the water, saffron, and cardamom in a saucepan over medium heat. Cover, and bring to a boil. Add tea bags, and let the tea steep for a minute, or longer if you like stronger tea. Strain into a cup, and sweeten with sugar if desired.

1720.title: Lemonade-Mint Iced Tea
1720.description: A refreshing and easy to prepare iced tea. You can vary the amounts of mint and sugar depending on your tastes.
ingredients: 1 (6 ounce) can frozen lemonade concentrate, thawed
instructions: In a 1 gallon pitcher, combine the mint leaves, 1 quart of boiling water, instant tea powder and sugar. Stir to dissolve sugar. Let stand for 15 minutes.
Stir in the cold water and lemonade concentrate. Serve in tall glasses over ice. Strain out mint leaves, if desired.

1721.title: Lemon-Ginger Iced Tea
1721.description: This lemon tea has just just a little kick to it because of the ginger. Serve over ice for a refreshing summer drink.
ingredients: 1 pinch white sugar, or to taste
0.5 cup brewed orange pekoe tea (such as Lipton®)
instructions: Bring water to a boil; add lemon-ginger tea bag. Let steep for 5 minutes. Sweeten with sugar and allow to cool.
Mix lemon-ginger tea and orange pekoe tea together and serve over ice.

1722.title: Peach Orange Iced Tea
1722.description: Peach-orange iced tea made with fresh peaches and oranges is a refreshing drink on hot summer days.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon white sugar, or to taste
instructions: Place peach, clementine, and sugar in a pitcher. Mash the fruit using a spoon; add water and tea bags and stir. Refrigerate until cool, about 1 hour. Remove fruit and tea bags using a slotted spoon.

1723.title: Peach Tea
1723.description: This is a very light tea with fresh peaches, great for a summer day.
ingredients: 2 fresh peaches - peeled, pitted, and sliced
instructions: Bring 3 cups water to a boil in a saucepan over high heat. Add the tea bags, and steep for 15 minutes. Remove tea bags.

Meanwhile, place peaches with 1 cup water into the jar of a blender, and blend until very smooth. Pour the peach mixture, tea, and stevia powder into a 1 gallon pitcher. Fill the pitcher to the top with water, and stir until blended.

1724.title: Cherry Ginger Infused Tea
1724.description: Fresh cherries and ginger infuse their flavors into a pitcher of green tea in this refreshing recipe.
ingredients: 1 (2 inch) piece fresh ginger, peeled and sliced
1 tablespoon lemon juice, or to taste
instructions: Combine cherries and ginger slices in a glass bowl. Sprinkle sugar over the cherries mixture and cover with 2 cups filtered water.
Cover bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate 2 hours to overnight.
Bring 2 cups filtered water nearly to a boil; pour over tea bags in a pitcher. Steep tea for 90 seconds. Squeeze tea bags into pitcher and discard bags.
Strain cherry-ginger water into pitcher with green tea, squeezing out excess liquid. Serve with lemon slices and lemon juice.

1725.title: Authentic Thai Iced Tea
1725.description: It's very easy to make authentic Thai iced tea at home, and it tastes so much better than using mixes or powders.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Thai tea leaves, or more to taste
0.66666668653488 cup white sugar, or to taste
instructions: Place tea leaves in a tea filter bag and secure.
Pour water into a pot and bring to a boil. Add tea bag and sugar. Return to a boil and stir until sugar has dissolved, about 3 minutes. Remove from heat and allow tea to steep for 30 minutes.
Discard tea bag. Let tea cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for 3 to 4 hours, or overnight.
Fill 2 glasses 2/3 full of chilled tea. Slowly pour 1/4 cup coconut milk into each glass.

1726.title: Cucumber Tea Spritzer
1726.description: Fresh cucumber, black tea, simple syrup, and carbonated water are combined to make these refreshing tea spritzers served over ice.
ingredients: 2 black tea bags, or more to taste
5 cups sparkling water, or as needed
instructions: Bring water to a boil in a kettle. Pour into a pitcher. Stir in sugar until it dissolves into a syrup. Add tea bags; let steep, about 5 minutes.
Fill 5 glasses with ice cubes. Add some cucumber slices. Fill glasses 3/4 full of sparking water. Divide sweet tea evenly among glasses. Squeeze some lemon juice into each drink; stir.

1727.title: Spiced Thai Iced Tea
1727.description: This iced tea spiced with star anise, cardamom, and cinnamon and sweetened with condensed milk is a sweet, refreshing Thai-inspired drink.
instructions: Place water, sugar, star anise, cinnamon stick, and cardamom in a saucepan; bring to a boil. Remove from heat and add tea bags. Let tea steep and cool to room temperature, about 1 hour.
Remove tea bags and strain out whole spices; discard. Whisk in condensed milk. Pour into a large pitcher and refrigerate until flavors combine, at least 1 hour.
Fill 4 glasses with ice. Serve tea over ice.

1728.title: Lemon Mint Iced Tea
1728.description: This refreshing iced tea is the perfect drink to serve at all your summertime parties. You can even make it in advance and keep it chilled in the refrigerator.
instructions: Bring the water to a boil in a large saucepan over high heat; remove from heat, then stir in sugar until dissolved. Add the tea and peppermint tea bags, and allow to steep for 30 minutes. Remove tea bag and stir in the lemonade. Serve tea over ice.

1729.title: Randy's Texas Tea
1729.description: Cold black tea with the refreshing tang of orange and lemon juices, a li'l sugah and the perfect garnish of sliced lemon and lime.
instructions: In a large pitcher, combine sugar, salt and hot water. Stir until completely dissolved. Sir in the tea, orange juice and lemon juice. Serve in tall glasses with ice and slices of citrus fruit.

1730.title: Thai Sweet Iced Tea
1730.description: Sweet and creamy Thai tea is a decadent drink spiced with cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon--perfect for sipping on a hot afternoon.
instructions: Bring water to a boil in a saucepan. Stir in tea leaves, vanilla extract, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon. Cover and remove from the heat. Let steep for 15 minutes.
Pour tea through a fine mesh strainer; discard tea leaves. Add sugar and stir until dissolved. Cover and chill in the refrigerator for 2 hours.
Fill glasses with crushed ice. Pour tea into glasses and top with half-and-half.

1731.title: Delicious Matcha Green Tea Frappuccino
1731.description: Inspired by the popular drink from Starbucks, this recipe provides a quick and less-expensive way to make a matcha green tea Frappuccino at home.
ingredients: 1 fluid ounce vanilla-flavored syrup (such as Torani®), or to taste
instructions: Blend ice, milk, vanilla syrup, and green tea powder together in a blender until smooth.

1732.title: Don's Simple Sweet Tea
1732.description: A simple sweet tea recipe that anyone can do. All you need is tea, water, and sugar!
instructions: Bring water to a boil in a pot. Dissolve sugar in boiling water; remove from heat.
Steep tea bags in water to desired strength of tea, 3 to 5 minutes.
Refrigerate tea until cold, at least 1 hour.

1733.title: Starbucks-Style Green Tea Frappuccino
1733.description: This copycat recipe uses matcha powder, coffee creamer, and xanthan gum to match the texture and flavor of Starbucks popular green tea drink.
instructions: Blend ice, milk, vanilla syrup, coffee creamer, green tea powder, and xanthan gum in a blender until smooth, 20 to 40 seconds.

1734.title: Raspberry-Apple Cider Iced Tea
1734.description: Ground ginger brings added flavor to this wholesome raspberry-apple cider iced tea drink that tastes as good as it makes you feel!
ingredients: 2 tablespoons organic apple cider vinegar with the mother
instructions: Place the tea bag into the boiling water and let steep for 5 minutes. Remove the bag.
Add 1 cup ice to a 32-ounce container and pour hot tea over top, stirring until all ice is melted. Add apple cider vinegar, stevia, and ginger; stir well. Serve over more ice.

1735.title: Dreamsicle Iced Tea Latte
1735.description: A sweet orange-flavored iced tea beverage with vanilla-almond syrup, this easy latte is made with almond milk and tastes like a dreamsicle.
instructions: Combine 1 cup water and brown sugar in a saucepan; bring to a boil, stirring frequently. Remove from heat; stir in almond extract and vanilla extract.
Combine remaining water and almond milk in a saucepan; bring to a boil. Add tea bags; steep for 5 minutes. Remove tea bags; stir in extract mixture. Fill two tall glasses with ice; pour in tea.

1736.title: Thai Iced Tea (Cha Yen)
1736.description: This sweet black tea mixed with evaporated milk and served over ice is a traditional, refreshing Thai drink perfect for a hot summer day.
instructions: Bring water to a boil in a small saucepan. Remove from heat and add black tea; let steep about 10 minutes or to desired strength.
Strain tea into a container and discard leaves. Add sugar and evaporated milk; stir until sugar is dissolved.
Fill 2 glasses with ice. Pour tea over ice. Top each glass with 1 1/2 teaspoon milk.

1737.title: Fresh Cranberry Spiced Tea
1737.description: A lovely clear red, hot beverage for holiday parties, an afternoon break, for dinner or bedtime as it contains no caffeine. I have been making this for decades and keep it in the fridge all winter. One of my most requested recipes!
ingredients: 2 cups white sugar, or to taste
instructions: Place the cranberries and water into a large pot. Bring to a boil and cook just until the berries pop, about 5 minutes. Remove from the heat and let stand at room temperature until cold, several hours.

Strain out the cranberries and stir the orange juice, pineapple juice, lemon juice and sugar into the liquid. Add the cinnamon stick, whole cloves and allspice berries. Bring to a low boil. It is ready to serve at this point, but it is even better if you allow it to sit overnight.

1738.title: Instant Pot® Iced Tea
1738.description: You can easily make homemade iced tea in your Instant Pot®. The tea and simple syrup are made at the same time!
instructions: Pour 5 cups of water into a multi-functional pressure cooker (such as Instant Pot®). Add sugar and tea bags. Close and lock the lid. Select high pressure according to manufacturer's instructions; set timer for 5 minutes. Allow 10 to 15 minutes for pressure to build.

Release pressure using the natural-release method according to manufacturer's instructions, for 15 minutes. Release remaining pressure carefully using the quick-release method, about 5 minutes. Unlock and remove the lid.
Remove tea bags and squeeze out remaining liquid into the pot. Pour tea into a pitcher and add remaining water. Serve over ice with lemon slices and mint sprigs.

1739.title: Lemon Almond Tea
1739.description: A refreshing iced tea to serve on hot summer days. Tea is flavored with lemon, almond and vanilla, then mixed with lemon-lime soda.
ingredients: 1 (2 liter) bottle lemon-lime flavored carbonated beverage, chilled
instructions: In a saucepan, brew tea bags in hot water for 15 minutes. While waiting for tea to brew, squeeze the lemon slices as you put them into a large pitcher. Pour in sugar.

Pour brewed tea into the pitcher with the sugar and lemons. You can let this sit in refrigerator for up to 1 day, or use it right away. When ready to serve, stir in almond extract, vanilla extract and lemon lime soda.

1740.title: Moji-Tea
1740.description: Minted iced tea with plenty of lemon and lime juice is a non-alcoholic version of a mojito. Add rum and club soda for an adult-version.
ingredients: 10 sprigs fresh mint, or more to taste
instructions: Place tea bags and mint sprigs in a large heat-proof measuring cup. Pour boiling water over tea bag mixture and cover measuring cup with a small plate. Steep tea until desired strength is reached, 15 to 20 minutes. Pour steeped tea through a strainer into a large mason jar, squeezing excess liquid from tea bags. Discard mint and tea bags.

Stir sugar into tea until dissolved; add lemon juice, lime juice, and vanilla extract. Stir cold water into tea mixture. Place lid on the jar and refrigerate until completely chilled, 2 hours to overnight.
Fill a punch bowl or drink dispenser with ice and add tea.

1741.title: Green Tea Berry Delight
1741.description: It doesn't get any simpler than pouring iced tea over frozen berries for a refreshing beverage.
instructions: Place the blueberries and strawberries in the bottom of a tall glass. Pour the green tea over the berries.

1742.title: Iced Tea III
1742.description: A cool, refreshing beverage of lemon-enhanced tea.
instructions: Place the tea bags and sugar into a 1 gallon glass jar. Fill with boiling water. Let steep for 2 hours at room temperature. Remove and discard tea bags. Stir in lemonade concentrate. Refrigerate until cool.

1743.title: Cranberry Orange Iced Tea
1743.description: When the temperature rises, stay cool with this cranberry and citrus iced tea.
ingredients: 9 packets Sweet'N Low granulated sugar substitute
instructions: In a large pitcher, pour the boiling water over the tea bags. Steep 5 minutes; remove the tea bags and discard.
Stir in the lemon juice and Sweet'N Low until the Sweet'N Low dissolves. Mix in the cold water and orange juice.
Refrigerate until well chilled.
Pour over ice in tall glasses.

1744.title: Instant Pot® Strawberry Iced Tea
1744.description: Use your Instant Pot® to make this big batch of iced tea flavored with fresh strawberry puree for a refreshing drink on a hot day.
instructions: Combine water, sugar, and tea bags in a multi-functional pressure cooker (such as Instant Pot®). Close and lock the lid. Select high pressure according to manufacturer's instructions; set timer for 4 minutes. Allow 25 minutes for pressure to build.
Release pressure carefully using the quick-release method according to manufacturer's instructions, about 5 minutes. Unlock and remove the lid. Remove tea bags using a slotted spoon.
Add strawberries to a blender and puree until smooth.
Allow tea to cool completely. Stir strawberry puree into the cooled tea and serve over ice.

1745.title: Springtime Citrus Cooler
1745.description: This is a refreshing, non-alcoholic cooler made with oranges, Earl Grey tea, and rose water. It is a springtime and summer favorite in our house, this citrus flavored drink refreshes nicely and serves as a great alternative to tea or water at a brunch.
instructions: Prepare a strong cup of tea with the Earl Grey, letting the bag steep for 5 minutes. Place the orange slices, sugar, rose water, and tea into a 1/2 gallon pitcher. Fill with cold water, and stir to dissolve the sugar.

1746.title: Delightful Punch
1746.description: A delightful punch made with tea, grapefruit, orange and pineapple juice. It's sweetened with simple syrup and carbonated with ginger ale. Note: make simple syrup by boiling equal parts water and sugar.
instructions: In a large punch bowl, combine tea, grapefruit juice, orange juice, pineapple juice and simple syrup. Stir in the ginger ale and serve.

1747.title: Iced Tea II
1747.description: Orange pekoe tea flavored with lemon juice and sweetened with sugar.
instructions: In a large saucepan, heat water to a rapid boil. Remove from heat and drop in the tea bags. Cover and let steep for 1 hour.
In a large pitcher, combine the steeped tea and the sugar. Stir until sugar is dissolved, then stir in lemon juice. Refrigerate until chilled.

1748.title: Instant Russian Tea
1748.description: This Russian tea is great for gifting! Include a tag with instructions so the recipient can mix up a cup of this mulled cider-like drink in an instant!
instructions: Combine both drink powders in a large bowl. Mix in sugar, tea powder, cinnamon, allspice, and cloves until well combined. Divide mixture among three pint-sized jars.
Write the following instructions on three gift tags: "Place 2 to 3 rounded teaspoonfuls into a cup, add boiling water, and serve."
Seal the jars and attach the gift tags.

1749.title: Classic Old Fashioned
1749.description: The old fashioned cocktail can be made with bourbon, rye, or blended whiskey. Serve over ice and garnish with an orange slice and a maraschino cherry.
instructions: Pour simple syrup, water, and bitters into a whiskey glass; stir to combine. Add ice cubes and pour in bourbon. Garnish with orange slice and maraschino cherry.

1750.title: Hot Toddy
1750.description: A hot toddy is a classic warm beverage made with whiskey and honey flavored with lemon, clove, cinnamon, and nutmeg for a cold weather pick-me-up.
instructions: Pour boiling water, whiskey, and honey into a mug. Add cloves, cinnamon, and lemon slice. Let mixture stand for 5 minutes so flavors can mingle, then sprinkle with a pinch of nutmeg before serving.

1751.title: Oolong, Orange, and Whiskey Punch
1751.description: Balanced with orange and a light touch of spice, this punch is whiskey-forward without being overpowering.
instructions: Bring water to a boil in a saucepan over high heat. Stir in sugar, cinnamon stick, and star anise. Remove from heat and add tea bags. Let steep for 3 minutes (or according to package directions for strongest tea). Remove tea bags. Let cool to room temperature, about 1 hour. Remove and discard cinnamon stick and star anise.
Stir together tea mixture, orange juice, whiskey, and lemon juice in a punch bowl or pitcher. Chill until cold, about 2 hours or up to overnight.
Garnish with tangerine slices and additional star anise. Ladle into ice-filled glasses. Top each with a tangerine slice.

1752.title: Homemade Irish Cream
1752.description: Irish cream liqueur made with whiskey, condensed milk, cream, and sugar with hints of coffee, chocolate, and almond for a sweet, creamy homemade beverage.
instructions: Gather all ingredients.

Combine sweetened condensed milk, Irish whiskey, heavy cream, chocolate syrup, coffee granules, vanilla, and almond extract in a blender. Blend on high speed until incorporated, 20 to 30 seconds. Store in a tightly sealed container in the refrigerator. Shake well before serving.

1753.title: Manhattan Cocktail
1753.description: A straightforward recipe for a Manhattan, made with rye whiskey, vermouth, a dash of bitters, and a maraschino cherry for a true classic cocktail.
instructions: Gather all ingredients.
Combine whiskey, vermouth, and bitters in a cocktail mixing glass. Add ice and stir until chilled.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass and garnish with a maraschino cherry.

1754.title: Old-Fashioned Swedish Glögg
1754.description: Glögg is a fragrant Swedish spiced wine punch spiked with whiskey and rum. You'll feel the heat when you serve this mulled wine for the holidays!
instructions: Heat port wine in a large stockpot with a lid over medium heat until just below the simmering point. Add bourbon and rum; heat until just below simmering. Save the bottles and their caps for storing leftover glögg.
Meanwhile, place cinnamon stick, orange peel, cloves, and cardamom pods in the center of the cheesecloth square. Gather edges of the cheesecloth and tie with kitchen twine to secure; set aside.

When wine mixture is very hot but not boiling, carefully light it with a long-handled match. Wearing a heatproof cooking mitt, carefully pour sugar into the flames; let mixture burn for 1 minute. Place the lid on the stockpot to extinguish the flames and turn off the heat. Let mixture cool, covered, about 10 minutes.
Add the cheesecloth spice bundle, raisins, and almonds to warm wine mixture; let it cool to room temperature, about 1 hour.
Strain cooled glögg and reserve the raisins and almonds.

To serve: Pour glögg into a saucepan and warm over medium-low heat until hot but not simmering, about 5 minutes. Ladle 3 ounces of warmed glögg into a small coffee cup or a small Swedish-style glögg mug, and garnish each serving with a few reserved raisins and almonds.

1755.title: Old Fashioned Cocktail
1755.description: This old fashioned cocktail recipe is a true classic made with a sugar cube muddled with bitters, then stirred with whiskey and a twist of lemon.
ingredients: 0.5 cup ice cubes, or as needed
instructions: Muddle sugar cube, water, and bitters in an old fashioned glass for 1 minute. Pour in whiskey; stir for 1 minute.
Squeeze lemon twist over the glass and drop it in. Add ice cubes. Garnish with orange slice and maraschino cherry; serve with a swizzle stick.

1756.title: Classic Whiskey Sour
1756.description: This lemon whiskey sour is made with your favorite whiskey, lemon juice, and simple syrup with maraschino cherries in this classic homemade cocktail.
ingredients: 1 cup ice cubes, or as needed
instructions: Combine whiskey, lemon juice, and simple syrup in a shaker. Fill with ice. Cover and shake until the shaker is frosty, about 30 seconds.
Strain into 3 martini glasses and garnish each glass with a maraschino cherry.

1757.title: The John Collins Cocktail
1757.description: The John Collins cocktail is made with bourbon instead of gin. It's flavored with lemon and topped up with club soda for a tall, iced cocktail.
instructions: Combine bourbon, lemon juice, and simple syrup in a cocktail shaker. Add 1 cup ice, cover, and shake until chilled. Strain into a Collins glass. Add 1 cup ice, fill with club soda, and stir.
Garnish with orange and lemon slices and a maraschino cherry.

1758.title: Maker's Mark Old Fashioned
1758.description: Straightforward and timeless, this Maker's Mark old-fashioned cocktail never goes out of style: a simple mix of bourbon, bitters, and sugar.
instructions: Muddle sugar, bitters, orange, cherry, and water in an old-fashioned glass.
Remove the orange rind and fill the glass 3/4 full of ice.
Add Maker's Mark Bourbon and stir.

1759.title: Mint Juleps
1759.description: Minty simple syrup mixed with bourbon becomes a refreshing mint julep with this simple recipe. It's a favorite for when you're watching the Kentucky Derby!
ingredients: 0.5 cup roughly chopped fresh mint leaves
8 cups crushed ice, or as needed
instructions: Make the simple syrup: Bring water, sugar, and chopped mint to a boil over high heat in a small saucepan. Cook, stirring occasionally, until sugar is completely dissolved, 1 to 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and let cool for 1 hour. Pour syrup through a strainer to remove mint leaves.
Make the cocktails: Fill eight glasses with crushed ice; pour 4 ounces bourbon and 1/4 cup mint syrup into each cup. (Add extra syrup for anyone with a sweet tooth.) Top each drink with a mint sprig.

1760.title: Southern Comfort Manhattan
1760.description: This Southern Comfort recipe makes a fabulous Manhattan cocktail with vermouth and aromatic bitters that's fruity, spicy, and incredibly delicious.
ingredients: 1 cup ice cubes, or as needed
2 (1.5 fluid ounce) jiggers Southern Comfort liqueur
instructions: Fill a cocktail shaker with ice. Pour in Southern Comfort, vermouth, and aromatic bitters. Cover and shake until the outside of the shaker has frosted. Strain into a highball glass with or without ice, then garnish with maraschino cherry.

1761.title: The Rusty Nail Cocktail
1761.description: Smoky Scotch gets sweetened up with the addition of Drambuie in the classic drink called the rusty nail.
instructions: Place 2 large ice cubes in a rocks class. Set aside in the freezer.
Combine Scotch and Drambuie in a cocktail mixing glass. Add 1/2 cup ice and stir until chilled. Strain into the chilled rocks glass.

1762.title: Bourbon Slush
1762.description: A fruity blend of juices, tea and bourbon whiskey are frozen into a slush, and then served topped off with lemon lime soda. This takes a while, but it's worth it!
ingredients: 1 (6 ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate
1 (2 liter) bottle lemon-lime flavored carbonated beverage
instructions: In a large bowl or container, mix together the orange juice concentrate, lemonade concentrate, pineapple juice, sugar, tea, and whiskey. Transfer to shallow bowls or dishes, and freeze overnight.

Remove the frozen mixture from the freezer and let stand for about 10 minutes. Chop with a wire whisk or potato masher to make a slushy consistency. Place scoops of the frozen slush into glasses, and top off with the lemon-lime flavored soda.

1763.title: True Manhattan
1763.description: This Manhattan recipe is the best! This classic cocktail can be served straight up or on the rocks. Most Manhattan drinkers like it stirred, not shaken.
ingredients: 1 cup ice cubes, or as needed
instructions: Fill a mixing glass with ice cubes. Pour in vermouth, then whiskey. Stir, then strain into a cocktail glass. Add bitters and garnish with cherry.

1764.title: Whiskey Sidecar
1764.description: This whiskey sidecar cocktail with lemon juice and orange liqueur swaps bourbon for cognac in this simple variation with a spicy, citrusy finish.
ingredients: 0.75 fluid ounce freshly squeezed lemon juice
instructions: Place sugar in a shallow bowl. Run a lemon wedge around the rim of a cocktail glass; dip the rim into sugar.
Combine whiskey, orange liqueur, and lemon juice in a cocktail shaker; add ice. Cover and shake until the outside of the shaker has frosted, about 20 seconds. Strain into the prepared cocktail glass.

1765.title: Irish Coffee
1765.description: Irish coffee is a classic after-dinner whiskey and coffee cocktail topped with whipped cream. Adding Irish cream liqueur makes it even more luxurious!
ingredients: 1 (1.5 fluid ounce) jigger Irish cream liqueur
instructions: Combine Irish cream liqueur and Irish whiskey in a glass mug; pour in hot brewed coffee. Top with whipped cream and a dash of nutmeg.

1766.title: 7 and 7
1766.description: This classic cocktail with 7UP and your favorite whiskey never goes out of style.
instructions: Serve over 1 cup of ice.

1767.title: Whiskey Slush
1767.description: A frozen whiskey-lemonade slush topped with ginger ale. Perfect for hot weather.
ingredients: 1 (12 fluid ounce) can frozen lemonade concentrate
1 (6 ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate
2 lemons - cut into wedges, for garnish
instructions: In a large plastic container combine lemonade concentrate, orange juice concentrate, tea, sugar, whiskey and water. Mix well and freeze for 24 hours.
Scoop into a tall glass, 3/4 full, and pour ginger ale to fill the glass. Stir and garnish with lemon wedges.

1768.title: Apple Jack
1768.description: I came up with this mix by accident when my bar tender misinterpreted me asking for a Jack and Pineapple juice by giving me a Jack and apple juice. It has since become a bar room staple.
instructions: Pour whiskey into a wide shot glass. Top with apple juice.

1769.title: Hot Irish Whiskey
1769.description: My best friend who just happens to be Irish made this drink for me one cold night in Chicago and since then, I have been hooked! Warning: it is very potent, just one of these will warm you up and basically make you good for nothing afterwards - what a treat! It is super to drink at night if you have a sore throat. My friend said this is what the Irish drink if they don't feel good but don't wait until you have a cold to try this recipe!
instructions: Press cloves into the peel of the lemon slice all the way around. Set aside. Measure the sugar into a wine glass. Place a metal spoon into the glass with the curved side facing upwards. Pour the boiling water over the back of the spoon. This will keep your wine glass from shattering. Stir to dissolve the sugar. Pour in the whiskey and add the lemon slice. Let steep for about 1 minute before drinking.

1770.title: Traditional Hot Toddy
